subject: Clarifications: MedBridge privacy questionnaire & data flow evidence
messages:
From: Samantha Pierce <samantha.pierce@medbridgehealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@medbridgehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: MedBridge privacy questionnaire v2 - clarifications and evidence request

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the fast turnaround on the privacy questionnaire. We reviewed the spreadsheet (attached) and have a few follow-up clarifications so our legal team can complete the RFI:

1) Cross-border transfers: can you confirm which legal transfer mechanisms Redwood relies on for EU->US and UK->US transfers today (e.g., SCCs, UK IDTA, DPF adequacy, or reliance on EU DPF)? We need explicit references to executed SCC versions if used.

2) Subprocessors and locations: please provide a current list of subprocessors that may handle Personal Data and the regions where processing occurs (cloud infra, logging/monitoring, analytics). 

3) Data mapping: we need a simple dataflow diagram (at a minimum, a map showing ingress, storage, inference runtime, logging/audit, backups) and a short note on what categories of personal data are stored persistently vs ephemeral only in memory.

4) Audit evidence: for SOC 2 and encryption-at-rest claims, please attach or link to the relevant artifacts, or tell us how we can request them.

5) Retention & deletion: confirm default retention for customer content and the workflows for deletion on contract termination.

Can you get these to us by EOD Friday (2026-11-06)? If you need more time, propose a date.

I'm attaching our latest questionnaire (medbridge-privacy-questionnaire-v2.xlsx) with in-line comments.

Best,
Samantha Pierce
Senior Counsel, Privacy
MedBridge Health

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Pierce <samantha.pierce@medbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedBridge privacy questionnaire v2 - clarifications and evidence request

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Stephanie (legal & contracts) and Marcus (infrastructure/privacy engineering) to make sure we cover the evidence side. Answers and artifacts below; I’ve attached a concise dataflow diagram and a DPA annex supplement.

1) Cross-border transfers
- Mechanisms: Redwood currently relies on the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) v2 (executed as part of our customer DPA) for EU->US transfers and the UK IDTA for UK->US transfers. We have an internal DPF (data protection framework) assessment memo for customers that elect to rely on SCCs; we do not self-certify under any government DPF adequacy mechanism.
- Reference: executed SCCs template used is our \"Redwood-SCCs-v2\" (we can append a redacted executed copy on request).

2) Subprocessors and locations
- Primary infra: AWS (us-west-2, eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west4) for model training/artifacts where applicable, and Azure (eastus) for certain dedicated customer projects.
- Observability/telemetry: Datadog (US), Sentry (US) — logs retained per contract (see retention section).
- Subprocessor list and last update: attached in DPA annex supplement (dpa-annex-supplement.docx). We can produce a live subprocessors CSV on request.

3) Data mapping / dataflow diagram
- Attached: redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf — shows ingestion (TLS), transient KV cache in GPU memory (not persisted by default), optional persistent logs and metrics (stored encrypted in S3/GCS), and backups (encrypted, limited TTL).
- Personal data categories: Account metadata (customer contact info) is persisted in our control plane DB; customer content submitted for inference is treated as Customer Content by default and kept ephemeral (processed in memory and KV caches), except where customers enable logging/retention or Dedicated deployments with storage enabled.

4) Audit evidence
- SOC 2: we maintain a SOC 2 Type II bundle — link to request via support portal. For a faster path, Stephanie can provide a redacted SOC 2 summary and encryption attestations.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest with KMS-managed keys (customer-managed KMS supported for Private deployments).

5) Retention & deletion
- Default: customer content ephemeral by default (24-hour KV cache TTL for hosted API), logs retained 90 days for observability (configurable), account metadata retained for the duration of the contract + 2 years unless otherwise specified.
- Deletion: standard deletion API and on-termination data purge workflow (documented) — we can provide the operational checklist.

Timeline: we can deliver the requested artifacts by EOD Thursday 2026-11-05 for the diagram and DPA supplement, SOC 2 evidence by next business day (subject to NDA), and a full subprocessors CSV by Monday 2026-11-09. Does that work?

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Legal Partnerships
Redwood Inference

[attachments: redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf, dpa-annex-supplement.docx]

Hi Grace / team — thank you, this is very helpful and aligns with what our GC was looking for. A couple of quick follow-ups before we close this out on our side: 

• Subprocessors: could you confirm whether any vendor has access to unredacted customer content for troubleshooting (i.e., are there break-glass processes or support-level access to content)? If so, how is access audited?
• SCCs: yes please provide a redacted executed SCCs copy — we only need the signature page and the governing law/annex references redacted where necessary.
• Timeline: the docs you offered (diagram + DPA supplement) are sufficient for our initial review. Please upload the SOC 2 summary and redacted SCCs to our secure Drive link and share the DocuSign/hubspot next steps for our procurement team.

We have one additional ask from procurement: a short summary line (1–2 sentences) confirming that Redwood does not perform transfers to third countries outside the subprocessors/regions previously listed without notice.

If you can push the requested artifacts to the Drive link and share a HubSpot record or DocuSign envelope by EOD today, we'll start the procurement review and loop in IT security for a final technical Q&A.

Thanks — Samantha

MedBridge Health
